[#reference-toolchain]
== The toolchain

What `agora` fetches for itself, because it has no Python wheel. Each entry is one exact version with an address and a SHA-256 for every platform it is built for, fetched into a per-user cache, checked before anything is unpacked, and tested after. `agora toolchain list` shows what your cache holds, and `agora help toolchain` explains the work.

=== Using a program of your own

Only when you name it. Each entry has a variable, and `doctor` lists every one that is set:

[cols="1,3"]
|===
|Variable |Stands in for

|`AGORA_ASCIIDOCTOR`
|an asciidoctor program

|`AGORA_ASCIIDOCTOR_PDF`
|a jar of asciidoctorj-pdf

|`AGORA_CHROMIUM`
|a Chromium or Chrome program

|`AGORA_JRE`
|the java program

|`AGORA_NPM_PACKAGES`
|a directory holding node_modules with playwright and @openedx/paragon

|`AGORA_TEX_PACKAGES`
|a TeX tree (its texmf-dist) holding the same packages

|`AGORA_TINYTEX`
|a directory holding xelatex and lualatex

|`AGORA_VSCE`
|a directory holding node_modules with @vscode/vsce and @vscode/test-electron

|`AGORA_VSCODE`
|a VS Code program

|===

=== System libraries

A browser and VS Code link shared libraries, and VS Code's tests need a display server, that a fetch cannot supply. `agora system add` installs them once with `sudo`: it prints exactly what it will run and asks first, and no other command uses `sudo`. The packages are pinned for Debian and Ubuntu; on another distribution it names the libraries and stops.
